blocks.text: Duplexes and half duplexes in Richmond
Local rules that affect duplexes in Richmond

items.t: Zoning (Richmond): Richmond Zoning Bylaw 8500 governs; houses across the residential districts sit in the Single Detached zones RS1 and RS2 (Section 8.1), with minimum lot areas by subzone including RS1/B 360.0 m², RS1/E 550.0 m², RS1/F 828.0 m² and RS1/K 315.0 m² and a 24.0 m minimum depth in most subzones. The OCP governing is Bylaw 9000 (2041). RSM SSMUH zones sit in the bylaw as amended. The zone and subzone of a specific lot are not confirmed until read — verify the lot's subzone minimums in Bylaw 8500 Section 8.1 before promising redevelopment value.

SSMUH position (Richmond): The City states it allows at least one secondary suite and/or accessory dwelling unit per lot on covered lots, with Bill 44 small-scale multi-unit minimums of 3 units on lots of 280 m² or less and 4 units on larger lots. A duplex is the baseline two-unit form inside that ladder. SSMUH adds unit potential on a lot; it does not by itself split a duplex into separately titled halves.
A secondary suite is a permitted secondary use in the RS1/RS2 zones; the Section 5.4 rules are at least 33.0 m², and at most the lesser of 40% of the dwelling floor area or 110 m².

Flood position (Richmond): All of Richmond is designated flood plain under the Flood Plain Designation and Protection Bylaw 8204, which sets dike setbacks and flood construction level (FCL) requirements. Flood construction level and insurance position are first-round diligence on any Richmond duplex.

faq.q: How big can a secondary suite in a Richmond duplex be?
faq.a: Section 5.4 of Bylaw 8500: At least 33.0 m², and at most the lesser of 40% of the dwelling floor area or 110 m².

faq.q: What flood diligence applies to a Richmond duplex?
faq.a: All of Richmond is designated flood plain under Bylaw 8204 — pull the property's flood construction level, dike-setback position and insurance terms in the first diligence round, against the 1:500-design dike system.

faq.q: When are property taxes due on a Richmond home?
faq.a: To the City of Richmond: for 2026, property taxes were due Thursday, July 2, 2026, with a 5% penalty on any unpaid balance after that date and a further 5% penalty on balances still outstanding after September 1, 2026.

Yes — Richmond is a low-lying island city in the Fraser River floodplain, protected by a perimeter dike system with drainage pump stations designed for a 1:500 flood event; the City is raising dikes from 3.5 metres to 4.7 metres for sea level rise, and Bylaw 8204 sets flood construction levels.

The Canada Line's Richmond–Brighouse branch serves Bridgeport, Aberdeen, Lansdowne and Richmond–Brighouse stations, and a second branch runs from Bridgeport to YVR–Airport, per TransLink's own service notice.
